The curious case of an alleged ghost attack at a Gozo residence has piqued the interest of a local group of paranormal investigators… and they’re ready to move in and do their thing.

“Following on what was reported on media today regarding the Gozo farmhouse, if the owner want us Malta Paranormal and GPI (Gozo Paranormal investigations) to perform a lock own investigation on the site, he’s/she’s more than welcome,” Malta Paranormal wrote on Facebook yesterday night.

The statement comes after news of the incident went viral. Allegedly, between the night of 22nd and 23rd September, a group of Maltese people staying at a Xewkija farmhouse experienced a number of bizarre and disturbing things they claimed were ghosts.

It started with one woman hearing someone call out for their mother, before seeing a human-like shadow beneath a dog, distressing their dog. Things allegedly escalated as the group attempted to leave. One man claimed a figure approached him from behind, grabbed him and repeatedly threw him against a bed. He reportedly described the figure as having a white face with no eyes and claimed it later appeared to pass through a closed glass door.The group also alleged that an oven door began violently opening and closing, a fan moved around the room as its cable was pulled, and buttons on a microwave appeared to activate on their own. No injuries were reported.

Lovin Malta contacted police over the unusual claims and can confirm that a 112 call was made, officers were dispatched to the residence and an official police report was subsequently filed. This confirms the police response and report, but not the alleged paranormal activity itself.

The group reportedly left the property after officers attended the scene, while a priest was said to have visited the residence several hours later.

Established in 2010, Malta Paranormal describes itself as the Maltese Division of the National Institute for Research and Studies of Paranormal Phenomena.
